members.title: Stern message from head of government
members.lead: After Ferdousi Ahmed (Misti), Ishraque Hossain has become the second person in two and a half weeks to be ordered to step down, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman sends a stern message to both the government and the party. According to assessments by senior figures in the government and the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), the message is not intended for the two individuals alone, but for ministers, members of parliament (MPs) and party leaders and activists alike. According to them, no one can be certain of retaining their position if they flaunt their power or embarrass the government and the party by overstepping the bounds of their responsibilities. Ferdousi Ahmed had to resign as an MP after people close to her were implicated in an attack on the Radda health centre in Mirpur, in the capital, and the demolition of its building. Ishraque, meanwhile, sparked controversy by taking part in an anti-narcotics operation while brandishing a firearm. In one case, questions were raised about the conduct of associates; in the other, the individual himself became the centre of controversy. . On Sunday afternoon, after a Cabinet meeting at the Secretariat, the prime minister summoned Ishraque and instructed him to resign. At a press conference at the National Press Club yesterday, Monday, Ishraque announced that he was stepping down as state minister. Earlier, following the prime minister’s instructions, Ferdousi Ahmed submitted her resignation to the Parliament Speaker on 1 October. Her parliamentary seat was subsequently declared vacant. . In their assessment, the main purpose of the tough decisions against Ishraque, following the action against Ferdousi Ahmed, was to prevent displays of arrogance in the exercise of power, ensure that people stayed within the limits of their mandate, and prevent individuals’ controversial actions from tarnishing the government and the party. . Following Ishraque’s resignation, this correspondent spoke to several members of the BNP…

members.title: Ishraque’s resignation accepted, gazette issued
members.lead: Ishraque Hossain’s resignation as state minister for liberation war affairs has been accepted. A gazette issued by the Cabinet Division on Tuesday said the President has accepted Ishraque’s resignation. On Monday around 2:30 pm, Ishraque announced his resignation as state minister at a press conference at the National Press Club in the capital. According to rules, the President accepts a resignation after it is submitted. The Cabinet Division then issues a gazette to this effect. .Ishraque loses ministerial position due to showy display of power. Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Ishraque is the member of parliament for Dhaka-6. On Saturday afternoon, he took part in an anti-drug drive in Gendaria, within his constituency, while carrying a firearm. After a video of the operation spread on social media, it sparked widespread discussion and criticism. This action of his while serving as the state minister for liberation war affairs caused discontent within the BNP and the government. Multiple government sources confirmed to Prothom Alo that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday instructed him to resign. .I apologise if I made a mistake, but I did nothing wrong: Ishraque. After news of the resignation order emerged, Ishraque denied it. His side issued a protest and threatened legal action also. He eventually announced his resignation as state minister at a press conference at the National Press Club on Monday afternoon. Later in the evening, a high level source in the Cabinet Division told Prothom Alo that it has received Ishraque’s resignation letter. Ahmed Azam Khan currently serves as the minister for liberation war affairs, with Ishraque having served as his state minister. Excluding the prime minister, the Cabinet had 26 full ministers and 24 state ministers. Following Ishraque’s resignation, the number of state ministers has fallen to 23.
